learning_outcomes.text: Be able to explain how different laser types operate and identify their key parameters
Be able to select an appropriate laser source for a given engineering application
Understand how laser parameters affect material processing and imaging performance
Be able to design basic experimental setups using lasers
Be equipped to evaluate technical literature and continue learning independently in photonics

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Why lasers matter in modern engineering
Fundamentals of laser light: coherence, spectra, beam shape
How lasers work: gain media, optical cavities, and amplification
Laser types: solid-state, gas, semiconductor, and fiber lasers
Applications: illumination for imaging, micro-machining, and remote sensing
Laboratory tutorials: laser operation and application demonstrations
bibliography: “Lasers : basics, advances and applications” - Springer, 2018 - H.J. Eichler, J. Eichler, O. Lux
“Photonics: Concepts, Technology and Applications” - Blackwell’s, 2019 - J. Landers
“Photonics, A Short course”- Springer, 2016 - V. Degiorgio, I. Christiani
“Fundamentals of photonics” - John Wiley and sons, Inc., 2019 - B. E. A. Saleh in M. C. Teich
“Applications of the Laser” - CRC Press, 2018 - L. Goldman
degree: Mechanical Engineering (2nd cycle, Erasmus+ subjects, Research and Development programme)
